gates.evidence: Both wrists show a real white textile facing above a plum sleeve. The white/plum boundary is clear, and the white fabric projects with thickness and shadow rather than looking printed. See both cuff crops.

The screen-left cuff has a doubled returning edge at its lower V-shaped opening; the screen-right cuff shows a rounded doubled lower turn. Inner and outer white surfaces meet around the opening with local thickness and a small occlusion shadow.

On each same sleeve, the visible inner white surface continues around the opening into the outward white facing lying over the plum exterior. The lower V on the screen-left sleeve and lower return on screen-right connect the inside surface to the outside facing in the same saved frame. The hands emerge from these openings, excluding a detached white glove reading.

limits: This qualifies only the visible local sleeve/lining fold, not a whole historical court ensemble or the historical term in all contexts.
Local visible continuity does not prove unseen tailoring construction, complete inner lining routes, era, rank or identity.
This record supplies no native typed-fact approval and does not activate a native obligation.
